While 'either... or' in natural language can sometimes imply exclusivity, in the context of formal logic and especially when comparing to the explicit exclusive OR operator (⊕), its absence makes the natural language ambiguous or more aligned with an inclusive OR. The FOL statement uses ⊕ (exclusive OR), which does not perfectly align with the typical interpretation of the given natural language without the 'but not both' clarification. If the NL intended exclusive OR, it should have been explicitly stated (e.g., 'It is not the case that Hottie either has strong instincts or is gentle, but not both'). Without that, the NL is more aligned with ¬(P ∨ Q) rather than ¬(P ⊕ Q).
